amendments.done_when: After a failed check or test, close's next round runs first the tests that failed, and runs no test again whose files are unchanged since its last pass; CI on the pull request still runs the full suite. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

done_when: After a failed test run, close's next round in a pytest repo runs the tests that failed first and skips tests whose files are unchanged since their last pass; other test tools rerun their full command as today; CI on the pull request still runs the full suite. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: Raise: Not done. A failed pytest case can disappear from the next close when the default branch advances. `close.py:403-405` fetches the latest default branch, and `close_test` at `review.py:252-258` embeds the new merge base in the fast-test command. This line keys failure receipts by that command, so the next close cannot see the earlier failure. If the repair restores the failed test file to base and leaves only a documentation change, the docs-only return at lines 277-283 reports success without retrying it; the picker can likewise select no test. The new evidence is a changed merge base between closes, which the restored-file test does not cover.
findings.title: Not done: advancing the merge base hides failed pytest cases

findings.body: Raise: Functional. In a pytest repo using `--cov=src --cov-fail-under=90`, a repair that changes a test or fixture can reuse most passing tests here. pytest-cov then measures only the tests actually run, so the repaired tests may pass while the configured coverage gate fails. [pytest-cov documents](https://pytest-cov.readthedocs.io/en/stable/config.html) that `--cov-fail-under` fails below the threshold and that prior coverage is discarded unless `--cov-append` is set. The end-to-end tests do not exercise a coverage-gated command.
findings.title: Coverage-gated pytest repairs stay red after their tests pass

findings.body: Raise: Scale. Every distinct expanded fast-test command gets a cache directory at `review.py:271-273`, and this code writes a full per-test JSON snapshot without removing old directories. The recommended `{base}` command changes as the default branch advances, leaving prior snapshots unused. A client with 10,000 tests and hundreds of pull requests accumulates hundreds of such snapshots in Forge's machine-wide config directory; the change has no cleanup path.
findings.title: Pytest receipt files grow without bound across pull requests

why: A repair round reruns everything even when one test failed
